annotatedSteps.description: Forming the first linear equation from the given conditions
annotatedSteps.studentWork:
Let number of correct answers = x and number of wrong answers = y.
3x + y = 40 ...(1)
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: × Incorrect equation: losing 1 mark means subtracting y, so it should be 3x - y = 40

annotatedSteps.description: Solving by substitution to find the value of x
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: ✓ Method and algebraic solution correct based on formed equations (ECF)
✓ Correctly evaluated y from the expression (ECF)

annotatedSteps.description: Finding the total number of questions
annotatedSteps.studentWork: ∴ Total number of questions = x + y = 13 + 1 = 14
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: ✓ Correct concluding step using calculated values (ECF)

teacherNote: Well done on clearly explaining your substitution method and solving the system with flawless algebra. Be careful when translating word problems into equations: losing marks means deducting them, so the first equation should be 3x - y = 40 instead of 3x + y = 40. Correct equations lead to x = 15, y = 5, and a total of 20 questions.
